children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful to know.

Could you tell me who Alex lives with? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex doesn't live with you at the moment, could you tell me a bit more about your situation?

Are you contributing towards the cost of looking after Alex (for example, paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his food, clothing, or other needs)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently contributing financially towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Could you tell me who Alex currently lives with and who is responsible for looking after him? For example, is he living with another family member, his other parent, or in some other arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Is Alex's other parent already claiming Child Benefit for him, or do you know if they intend to?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if they're already claiming it or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Just a couple more questions to make sure I have the full picture:

Are you a UK resident? (For example, do you live in England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me summarise:

- Alex is 6 years old
- He does not live with you
- You are not currently contributing financially towards his upkeep
- He lives with his other parent
- You are a UK resident

Let me now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you must either:
1. Have the child living with you, **or**
2. Be contributing towards the cost of looking after the child (at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount)

Since Alex lives with his other parent and you are not currently contributing financially towards his care, you do not meet either of these conditions.

**What this means:**

Alex's other parent (the person he lives with) would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for him. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time.

**If your circumstances change:**

If Alex comes to live with you in the future, or if you start contributing financially towards his upkeep at a level at least equal to the Child Benefit rate, you may become eligible at that point.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?
